title: What If You Could Never Feel Pain?

scenes.text: What if you could never feel pain? It sounds like a superpower. Doctors say it is the opposite.
It is real: congenital insensitivity to pain, so rare that the UK has known of fewer than thirty cases.
In the first years of life, children can injure their mouths and fingers by repeated biting, because nothing tells them to stop.
Burns go unnoticed too. Without the warning, a hot drink or a hot surface can injure before anyone realises.
Over the years, broken bones and damaged joints pile up unnoticed, and joint damage is almost universal in older patients.
Repeated injuries often shorten life. Pain is not a flaw. It is the alarm that keeps us alive.

description:
What if you could never feel pain?
Congenital insensitivity to pain is real and rare: unnoticed injuries, burns, bone and joint damage, and often a shorter life. Pain is the body's alarm.
